title: The Wind-Sons: Bhima and Hanuman
body:
The Wind-Sons: Bhima and Hanuman

न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ।।

"Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings; nor in the future shall any of us cease to be. (Gita II-12)"

During their stay in the Himalayan heights, a north-east breeze wafted a beautiful, fragrant flower near Draupadi. Captivated by its celestial scent and beauty, she showed it to Bhima, requesting him to find the plant so they could grow it in their Kamyaka forest. Anxious to please his beloved, Bhima strode off towards the north-east, following the fragrance without a thought of the wild beasts crossing his path.
Deep in a banana grove, Bhima saw a huge, old monkey lying directly across his path. Bhima shouted at the animal, commanding it to move, to which the monkey drawled: 'I am old and indisposed; why did you wake me? If you have scruples about jumping over me, kindly push my tail aside and proceed.' Bhima, proud of his immense physical strength, attempted to pull the monkey out of the way by its tail.
To his utter amazement, Bhima could not move the tail even a hair's breadth. He set his jaws and strained every muscle until his body was covered in sweat, but the tail remained as solid as a mountain. In deep humility, Bhima bowed before the monkey, asking: 'Who are you? Forgive my pride and reveal your divine identity.' The monkey smiled and revealed himself as Hanuman, Bhima's older spiritual brother, both born of the Wind God. Hanuman blessed Bhima, promising to sit atop Arjuna's chariot flag during the war to strike terror into the hearts of their enemies—a profound lesson in physical and spiritual humility.
